items.prompt: [S1] In a school, the number of boys : number of girls = 5 : 7. There are 24 more girls than boys. Find the total number of students.
items.solution:
Difference in parts = 7 − 5 = 2 parts.
2 parts = 24, so 1 part = 12.
Total = 12 parts = 12 × 12 = 144 students.

items.prompt: [S2] A ladder 13 m long leans against a vertical wall. The foot of the ladder is 5 m from the wall. Find the height reached by the top of the ladder, in metres.
items.solution:
By Pythagoras’ theorem, height² = 13² − 5² = 169 − 25 = 144.
Height = 12 m.

items.prompt:
[S1] The mean of seven numbers is 7. Six of the numbers are 3, 5, 5, 7, 9 and 12.
(a) Find the seventh number.
items.solution:
Sum of 7 numbers = 7 × 7 = 49.
Sum of the six given numbers = 3 + 5 + 5 + 7 + 9 + 12 = 41.
Seventh number = 49 − 41 = 8.
items.stem: The mean of seven numbers is 7. Six of the numbers are 3, 5, 5, 7, 9 and 12.

items.prompt: [S2] A concert sells 30 tickets in total. An adult ticket costs $80 and a child ticket costs $50. The total income is $1830. Find the number of adult tickets and the number of child tickets sold.
items.solution:
Let a and c be the numbers of adult and child tickets.
a + c = 30 and 80a + 50c = 1830.
c = 30 − a: 80a + 50(30 − a) = 1830
80a + 1500 − 50a = 1830
30a = 330 → a = 11.
11 adult tickets and 19 child tickets.
Check: 80(11) + 50(19) = 880 + 950 = 1830.

items.prompt: [S2] (a) Expand (2x − 3)².
[S2] (b) Factorise 6x² − x − 12.
items.solution:
Numbers with product 6 × (−12) = −72 and sum −1 are −9 and 8.
6x² − 9x + 8x − 12 = 3x(2x − 3) + 4(2x − 3) = (3x + 4)(2x − 3).

items.prompt: [S2] (c) Hence solve (2x − 3)² = (3x + 4)(2x − 3).
items.solution:
(2x − 3)² − (3x + 4)(2x − 3) = 0
(2x − 3)[(2x − 3) − (3x + 4)] = 0
(2x − 3)(−x − 7) = 0
x = 3/2 or x = −7.
Do not divide both sides by (2x − 3): that would lose the root x = 3/2.

[S2] A cylindrical water tank has base radius 0.6 m and height 1.5 m.
(a) Find the capacity of the tank in m³, correct to 3 significant figures.
items.stem: A cylindrical water tank has base radius 0.6 m and height 1.5 m.

items.prompt:
[S2] A cylindrical water tank has base radius 0.6 m and height 1.5 m.
(b) Water flows into the empty tank at 12 litres per minute. Find the time needed to fill the tank, in minutes correct to the nearest minute.
items.solution:
1 m³ = 1000 L, so capacity = 540π ≈ 1696.5 L.
Time = 540π ÷ 12 = 45π ≈ 141.37… ≈ 141 minutes.
(Accept 2.4 hours or 2 h 21 min.)

items.prompt:
[S2] A cylindrical water tank has base radius 0.6 m and height 1.5 m.
(c) The curved surface of the tank is to be painted at $45 per m². Find the cost, correct to the nearest dollar.
items.solution:
Curved surface area = 2πrh = 2π(0.6)(1.5) = 1.8π ≈ 5.655 m².
Cost = 1.8π × 45 = 81π ≈ 254.47… → $255 (nearest dollar).

items.prompt:
[S2] Tap A alone can fill a tank in 12 minutes. Tap B alone can fill the same tank in 18 minutes.
(a) Find the fraction of the tank filled in 1 minute when both taps are opened.
items.solution:
A fills 1/12 of the tank per minute; B fills 1/18.
1/12 + 1/18 = 3/36 + 2/36 = 5/36.
So 5/36 of the tank is filled per minute.
items.stem: Tap A alone can fill a tank in 12 minutes. Tap B alone can fill the same tank in 18 minutes.

items.prompt:
[S2] Tap A alone can fill a tank in 12 minutes. Tap B alone can fill the same tank in 18 minutes.
(b) Both taps are opened together for 4 minutes. Tap A is then closed and tap B continues until the tank is full. Find the total time taken to fill the tank, in minutes.
items.solution:
In 4 minutes: 4 × 5/36 = 20/36 = 5/9 of the tank.
Remaining = 1 − 5/9 = 4/9.
Time for B = (4/9) ÷ (1/18) = (4/9) × 18 = 8 minutes.
Total time = 4 + 8 = 12 minutes.
items.stem: Tap A alone can fill a tank in 12 minutes. Tap B alone can fill the same tank in 18 minutes.

items.prompt:
[S2] In △ABC, ∠A = 90°, AB = 8 cm and AC = 6 cm. D is a point on BC such that AD ⊥ BC.
(b) Find the area of △ABC, in cm², and hence find AD, in cm. Give the area and AD in that order (e.g. 24, 4.8).
items.solution:
Area = ½ × 8 × 6 = 24 cm².
Also Area = ½ × BC × AD = ½ × 10 × AD, so 5·AD = 24.
AD = 4.8 cm.
items.stem: In △ABC, ∠A = 90°, AB = 8 cm and AC = 6 cm. D is a point on BC such that AD ⊥ BC.

items.prompt:
[S2] In △ABC, ∠A = 90°, AB = 8 cm and AC = 6 cm. D is a point on BC such that AD ⊥ BC. (It has been found that BC = 10 cm and AD = 4.8 cm.)
(c) Find BD and DC, in cm. Give BD and DC in that order (e.g. 6.4, 3.6).
items.solution:
In right △ABD: BD² = AB² − AD² = 64 − 23.04 = 40.96.
BD = 6.4 cm.
DC = 10 − 6.4 = 3.6 cm.
items.stem: In △ABC, ∠A = 90°, AB = 8 cm and AC = 6 cm. D is a point on BC such that AD ⊥ BC.

items.prompt:
[S2] In △ABC, ∠A = 90°, AB = 8 cm and AC = 6 cm. D is a point on BC such that AD ⊥ BC.
(d) Prove that △ABD is similar to △CAD.
items.solution:
∠ADB = ∠CDA = 90° (given AD ⊥ BC).
In △ABC, ∠B + ∠C = 90°; in △ABD, ∠BAD = 90° − ∠B, so ∠BAD = ∠C = ∠ACD.
Two pairs of equal angles ⇒ △ABD ~ △CAD (AA).
(Consistency check: AD/DC = 4.8/3.6 = 4/3 and BD/AD = 6.4/4.8 = 4/3. Also AD² = BD × DC.)
acceptedAnswers: triangle ABD similar to triangle CAD
items.stem: In △ABC, ∠A = 90°, AB = 8 cm and AC = 6 cm. D is a point on BC such that AD ⊥ BC.

items.prompt:
[S1] The test marks (out of 100) of two classes are shown below.
Class A: 52, 65, 68, 70, 72, 75, 78, 80, 85, 95
Class B: 60, 62, 66, 70, 74, 74, 76, 78, 80, 90
(a) Find the mean and the median of each class. Give mean A, median A, mean B, median B in that order (e.g. 74, 73.5, 73, 74).
items.solution:
Class A: total = 740, mean = 74; median = (72 + 75)/2 = 73.5.
Class B: total = 730, mean = 73; median = (74 + 74)/2 = 74.

items.prompt:
[S1] The test marks of Class A have mean 74 and median 73.5; Class B have mean 73 and median 74.
(b) The principal says “Class A did better because its mean is higher.” Comment on this statement using these results.
items.answer: Not fully justified: A has higher mean but lower median
items.solution: Class A has the higher mean but the lower median, so the two classes are in fact very close. Class B’s higher median means its “middle” student scored higher, i.e. Class B is more consistent at the centre; the statement is therefore not fully justified.
